articleTitle: Novel high-frequency continuous-time low-pass OTA based filters
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A novel second-order low-pass operational transconductance amplifier (OTA)-based filter is described. In addition to its simplicity, the circuit exhibits the following attractive features: use of grounded and equal valued capacitors throughout, low sensitivity to passive component tolerances, and good high-frequency operation as shown by a 2.5-MHz Butterworth filter design. The simplicity of the CMOS implementation of such a filter is evident when compared with that of other low-pass filters reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of 2-D recursive digital filters in the spatial domain
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A class of least-squares algorithms for designing two-dimensional digital filters from space-domain data is presented. The proposed algorithms iteratively estimate the filter coefficients by minimizing the true squared error between the given and the estimated space-domain responses. The algorithms are essentially generalizations of the optimal 1-D design algorithm given by A.G. Evans and R. Fischl (1973). The error criterion is simultaneously optimized with respect to the coefficients in both dimensions. Design algorithms are given for filters with separable and irreducible numerator/denominator polynomials and also for mixed structures. The effectiveness of the algorithms is illustrated with several simulation examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Configuration and performance of modulated filter banks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The performance issues relating to the transmultiplexers previously synthesized by the authors (see Proc. IEEE Int. Conf. Acoust., Speech, and Signal Processing, Albuquerque, NM, April 1990) are examined. The transmultiplexers consist of modulated filter banks based on one or two low-pass prototypes. The limitations of the configured systems regarding intersymbol interference and crosstalk suppression arising from the use of practical filters are analyzed. Based on these observations, a design technique for FIR (finite-impulse response) prototypes that takes the practical degradations into account is formulated. The procedure involves the unconstrained optimization of an error function. The resulting performance is compared with minimax filters. For the one-prototype systems, the method is superior because it leads to better intersymbol interference and crosstalk suppression with a smaller number of filter taps. In the case of the transmultiplexer with two prototypes, the main advantage of the design method is the inclusion of crosstalk terms in the error function. It is noted that the five transmultiplexers can be converted into subband systems. How the design approach formulated for transmultiplexers carries over to the subband systems is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A model generation and compilation system for improving electrical performance
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The EPOXY system statically builds the equations that model circuit performance and sensitivity information. Although this approach requires more memory, the computation involved in evaluating circuit performance is significantly reduced. These equations are compiled internally for even faster evaluation. Transistor sizing alone may not be sufficient for meeting the required performance goals for a defined functional block. Therefore, this system considers local circuit changes such as inserting buffer stages, rearranging transistors within a pull-up or pull-down tree, and splitting large transistors so that cell height and width can be traded off. These circuit changes are implemented by directly modifying the performance equations. The benefits of deriving a static set of performance equations are described. Since compiling the performance equations offers a tremendous reduction in the overall running time, an examination is made of how EPOXY copes with the problems associated with feedback in a circuit and circuit-level modifications. Issues dealing with the equation aspects of formulating the transistor sizing program as a nonlinear optimization problem are presented. A discussion is presented of several evaluation techniques that are supported by EPOXY's internal compiler. Execution times and storage requirements are evaluated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transputer based back-propagation neural net emulation system
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A transputer based back-propagation neural net emulation system is presented. The authors propose one mapping approach for mesh architecture. The major challenge of this research work is to map the back-propagation neural net model onto transputer arrays for mesh architecture. The OCCAM parallel programming language is used for programming the operations of these transputers. Using this transputer based emulation system, a test case for Mandarin (Chinese voice) speech zero to nine recognition is implemented, and encouraging results, i.e. the recognition rate of inside test 99% and outside test 96%, have been obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiplexing of luminance and chrominance in NTSC compatible extended definition systems based on subsampling
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Methods are presented for luminance-chrominance multiplexing in an NTSC (National Television System Committee) compatible extended-definition transmission scheme based on subsampling. A one-dimensional multiplexing scheme has been illustrated with a 4:1 interlaced sampling structure based on HD-MAC. This one-dimensional multiplexing scheme can also be used with the Triscan 6:1 interlaced sampling structure in a straightforward way. A two-dimensional multiplexing scheme has also been illustrated, this time using a modified Triscan sampling structure. These techniques allow methods similar to those proposed in Europe for HDTV (high-definition television) broadcasting to be used with the NTSC system. Then, all the techniques which have been developed for compatible HD-MAC to improve the quality of the compatible picture and to improve motion rendition in the HD picture can be brought to bear on this scheme. These include preprocessing and postprocessing to reduce flicker in the compatible image and motion-compensated processing for improved interpolation and moving areas in the HD picture.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel computation of fan-beam back-projection reconstruction algorithm in computed tomography
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A method for parallelizing the image reconstruction of a fan beam computed tomography (CT) scanner and a processor array adapted for computing the back-projection reconstruction algorithm (BPR) are presented. By making use of some inherent parallelism in PBR, a modular ring architecture in multiple of eight processors is shown to be well suited for a class of CT algorithms. The parallel architecture encompasses a reconfigurable binary tree to accommodate a wide range of processor interconnections needed for different image-processing schemes, ranging from front-end filtering, calibration, and fast Fourier transform to postprocessing such as artifact removal and image compression.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Base resistance and pn junction capacitance extraction on vertical bipolar transistors
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The general concepts of base resistance and pn junction capacitance extraction are discussed. A formulation that can be adopted to extract the base resistance for typical transistor structures is reviewed. A formulation for the calculation of zero-bias space-charge-region capacitances of pn junctions is introduced. A general-purpose bipolar transistor simulator is used to extract both the base resistance and the pn junction capacitances of arbitrarily shaped bipolar transistors based on the formulations. Simulated results are in good agreement with values obtained using high-precision measurement techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Tradeoffs in partitioning for waveform relaxation on multicomputers
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A study of static circuit partitioning algorithms for waveform relaxation (WR) on a multicomputer is presented. For such a computer there is an important tradeoff between the irregularity in partitioning and the achievable parallelism. Also, the importance of accuracy in certain steps in the partitioning calculation has been investigated. Topological methods are compared with several other methods which try to estimate the convergence factor for the WR iterations. For digital CMOS circuits it is found that only the close neighborhood to a circuit node (nearest neighbors) influences the value of the worst-case coupling. The conductive coupling is the essential part to consider in the partitioning. For a few circuits (mostly circuits with cross-coupling) the capacitive coupling must also be included in the partitioning. It is, however, hard to find an exact limit for the convergence factor estimate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A speech processing LSI for ATM network subscriber circuits
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A signal-processing large-scale integration (LSI) configuration and its advantages with respect to speech communications subscriber circuits on an asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) network are described. The LSI configuration combines the silence span compression/expansion function and the cell loss compensation function into a single group of three LSI chips which are capable of processing media for both pulse code modulation (PCM) and adaptive differential PCM (ADPCM) environments. A near-end echo canceller with a single speech-processing LSI which serves to absorb delays in voice packeting, as well as to absorb the influence of cell propagation delays, is described. A performance evaluation is presented. The results indicate that good speech quality can be realized on an ATM network up to cell loss rate of about 3% for ADPCM speech, and about 8% for PCM speech.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Layered neural networks applied to the recognition of voiceless unaspirated stops
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The behavior of layered neural nets when they are applied to speech recognition is studied. The input to the neural net is a feature vector which describes the characteristics of the voiceless unaspirated stops. The function of the neural net is to classify the articulation place of the stop consonants. In this study, the neural network classifier is compared with the Bayes classifier to reveal the advantages gained by using a neural network as a classifier. The effect of the number of the processing units in the hidden layer is examined. A method of minimizing the degradation in performance of an existing neural net when one of the hidden processing units misses is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An optimization scheme for locating power system equilibria ranked by a scalar Lyapunov function
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A constrained optimization algorithm for implementing a geometric approach to ranking UEPs (unstable equilibrium points) is proposed. The formulation seeks to minimize a Euclidean norm of the vector field along a constraint manifold defined by a constant contour of the Lyapunov function. When the norm is driven to zero on the manifold, one has located an equilibrium point having the given value of energy. A scheme for modifying the constraint contour is proposed, and a limit on the number of local minima in a neighborhood of the operating point is demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computation of large-change sensitivity of cascade networks
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An explicit formula and an iterative algorithm of the large-change sensitivity of cascade networks are given. Some properties of cascade networks are discussed and used to simplify the calculation of the large-change sensitivity. The results are useful for designing active or passive networks and filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of three-dimensional digital filters based on the outer product expansion
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An efficient design method for three-dimensional digital filters by outer product expansion is proposed. Specifications of three-dimensional digital filters are decomposed into specifications of one-dimensional digital filters by the outer product expansion, and each specification of one-dimensional digital filters is designed. This procedure can be applied to both space-domain and frequency-domain specifications. Diagonal symmetries of three-dimensional digital filters can be exploited to reduce computations in the design procedure. The parallel separable structure produced by this method has high parallelism, regularity and modularity, making it suitable for parallel and VLSI implementation of 3-D digital filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Foundations of cone-beam tomography
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A nonmathematical review of recent developments in the theory of cone-beam tomography is presented. The completeness condition and three novel reconstruction formulas are reviewed. Using this theory in medical applications is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analysis of coefficient inaccuracy for 2-D FIR direct form digital filters
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An analysis is presented of filter frequency errors due to coefficient quantization in direct-form realizations of zero-phase two-dimensional finite-impulse response (2-D FIR) digital filters. Applying a method already used for 1-D FIR digital filters, the case of 2-D FIR filters with octagonal or quadrantal symmetry is considered. Based on the analysis, statistical bounds on the frequency-response errors and on the word length of the filter coefficients are developed and verified by experimental data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Decomposition of the focusing transformation in coherent signal-subspace DOA estimation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A decomposition of the focusing transformation matrix needed in the coherent signal-subspace method of H. Wang and M. Kaveh (IEEE Trans. ASSP, vol.ASSP-33, no.4, p.823-31, Aug. 1985) is presented. The decomposition yields a structure for implementing the space-time domain filter needed to preprocess the array data prior to the direction of arrival (DOA) estimation step. The resulting structure uses blocking matrices and steering matrices as modules to give a simples preprocessing filter. This structure is compared to a previously published multichannel filter design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of a fast codebook searching algorithm using a neural-network model
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The design of a fast codebook searching algorithm using a neural network perceptron model is described. The design of the codebook containing the optimal number of representative vectors incorporates a tree structure with a modified perceptron neuron at each node. The proposed algorithm reduces the computational requirements compared to the full-search and tree-search algorithm and requires less memory than the tree-search algorithm. The implementation of a neural vector pattern matching system using the tree-searched neural vector quantisation algorithm as a building block is discussed briefly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Matrix permutations of mesh-connected arrays
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Square systolic arrays for performing a class of matrix permutations are presented. This class can be described by the composition of two basic operations, namely clockwise rotation by 90 degrees , and horizontal reflection about the middle column. Four different arrays are presented: in-place reflection, in-place rotation, and on-the-fly versions of these that permute the matrix as it is being loaded into the array. These operations can be implemented very efficiently with local only control. The time bounds for each of the operations is optimal.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 5 ns 1 Mb BiCMOS SRAM with ECL I/O interface
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A high-speed X-address decoding scheme with wired-OR bipolar predecoders and partial decoding level converters is presented. In addition, a sensing scheme with small signal voltage swing (particularly for read bus lines) is described. These two high-speed schemes and a double-level polysilicon layer, double-level metal layer, 0.8- mu m BiCMOS process technology were used to implement a 5-ns address access time, 1-W power dissipation, and 1-Mb emitter-coupled logic input/output (I/O) interface SRAM (static random-access memory).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A technique for constructing an initial point for solving a system of linear equations by iterative methods
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Iterative methods for solving systems of linear equations are attractive because of their simplicity. A fundamental problem of iterative solution methods is the requirement of an initial guess as a starting point. A technique is described for constructing a nontrivial initial point to accelerate the convergence of iterative methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hyperbolic rotation of subspaces and VLSI algorithms for signal processing and numerical linear algebra
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Starting from the viewpoint of linear physical systems, a brief study is presented of energy-conserving or J-orthogonal transformations in a space with an indefinite metric under the special aspect of their VLSI realization. A mesh-connected array of n/sup 2/ processor cells, each performing a plane hyperbolic rotation, is shown to be the most natural of n-dimensional subspaces. Isometric linear fractional maps of contractive matrices to the zero matrix and hyperbolic Cholesky factorization are presented as the most interesting applications in generalized Schur methods, digital signal processing, and numerical linear algebra. Using the Cholesky factorization as an example, a square-root- and division-free computation scheme for hyperbolic rotations that is highly suited for VLSI implementation is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On-line security classification using an artificial neural network
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A neural network classifier for the class of problems associated with transmission-line faults is described. Faults are considered to be modeled by continuous parameters. The solution is then embedded in a set that results from a map of the current stable equilibrium point to the set of all 4-cycle-fault-on post-fault operating points. An experimental analysis of the application of a single-layer feedforward network to the problem of security screening is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new scheme of implementing N-port circulator with summers
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A scheme for implementing a N-port circulator using summers is presented. This philosophy can be adopted in both the analog and digital implementation of an N-port circulator. For the analog case, a compensation type summer with minimum phase error is presented. A three-port circulator for an ISDN basic access hybrid circuit is given as an example. It is integratable and has minimum phase error.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of the VQ based image coding algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Four objective measures and a subjective measure are used to evaluate the images reconstructed by a mean/quantized residual vector quantizer (MQRVQ) algorithm. These reconstructed images are also evaluated using a subjective evaluation method recommended by the international radio consulting committee. The subjective test results are analyzed. The strength of MQRVQ in coding high-detail pictures and texts is supported by the subjective ratings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new placement algorithm for custom chip design
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A placement algorithm which consists of three subalgorithms-an O(kn/sup 2/) circle model relative placement algorithm, an O(n/sup 2/ log n) triangulation algorithm, and an O(n/sup 2/ log n/sup 2/) optimal slicing algorithm for custom chip design-is presented. This relative placement algorithm addresses size effect and net connectivity effect simultaneously, while attaining a low polynomial time complexity O(kn/sup 2/) without loss of global perspective, where k is a constant and depends on the accuracy that the placement required. The triangulation algorithm has O(n/sup 2/ log n) time complexity. The triangulated planar graph can be used to do the floorplan be either the nonslicing RDG (rectangular dual graph) or slicing embedding methods. The optimum slicing algorithm has O(n/sup 2/ log n/sup 2/) time complexity. As expected, the wire length of the placement algorithm is shorter than that of a point model. However, since the optimal values of l/sub 0/ and DEF (deformation ratio) are unknown, different values for l/sub 0/ and DEF should be used in different circuits to obtain better placement results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coplanar Schottky waveguides for microwave phase shifting, attenuation and harmonic generation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A coplanar Schottky waveguide device developed for phase shifting, attenuation, and harmonic generation applications in the microwave region is described. The device has micron size features, and has the added advantage of low cost, small size, and simple structure. It has the unique feature of combining several circuit functions into one elemental device. The theory, fabrication and design, and experimental results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Existence, uniqueness and determination of solution of certain piecewise linear resistive networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: For an equation of the form F(x)=y, it is shown that there is at least one solution for every y if F is eventually P/sub 0/ passive or the effective Jacobian matrix in all the unbounded regions is a P matrix. In addition to this, if the Jacobian determinant has the same sign in all the regions, then F is a homeomorphism. For equations of the form F(x)=g(x)+Hx=y, F(x) is onto if H is P/sub 0/ and F(x) is norm coercive where g(x) is diagonal. This statement is true for equations of the form F(x)=Ag(x)+Bx=y also where (A,B) is W/sub 0/. In these results g/sub 1/(x1) is allowed to saturate without requiring additional conditions on H or (AB). It is also shown that, roughly under these conditions, the generalized Katzenelson's method converges to a solution. Homeomorphism of these two forms is guaranteed if the Jacobian determinant has the same sign in all the regions in addition to the above conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transfinite resistive networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Transfinite electrical networks are infinite networks in which some of the nodes are connected by infinite paths but not by finite ones. Such networks arise naturally as certain transitional cases between lumped and distributed networks, but to date neither a definition nor a fundamental theory existed for them. The structure of such networks is explicated, and some foundational theorems for the existence of unique voltage-current regimes in resistive infinite networks are stated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal flow graph based synthesis of strays-insensitive switched-capacitor filters
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An algorithmic method of designing biphase-clocked strays-insensitive switched-capacitor filters is presented. The desired transfer function is mapped on a general signal-flow graph, which is composed of branches that represent the signal flow in elementary strays-insensitive switched-capacitor structures. Translating this type of graph into switched-capacitor filters yields circuits with a number of attractive properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Compensation of sample-and-hold distortion through zero insertion
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An analytic method for the compensation of the (sin x)/x distortion inherent to digital or sampled-data systems with continuous-time output signals is presented. The compensation is achieved through the insertion of a pair of finite zeros in the transfer function of the system. Simple expressions are provided for the calculation of the magnitude and the Q-factor of the zeros of the compensation function. An example illustrates the efficiency and the applicability of the method. Simulation results are presented for a second-order Chebyshev filter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A CMOS class-AB transconductance amplifier for switched-capacitor applications
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A CMOS operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using a fully differential single-stage core OTA as the input stage and a differential to single current converter as the output stage, each biased at a separate current level, is presented. A large gain-bandwidth product (2.7 MHz) and a high slew-rate (5 V/ mu s) can be obtained by applying a large bias current to the core OTA. Due to the class-AB operation of the output stage, a high output impedance can be obtained by applying a small bias current to the output stage, resulting in a high DC-gain (61.6 dB). When the performance of this class-AB OTA is compared with that of basic single-stage OTAs it is found that the output impedance of the class-AB OTA is increased without limiting the bandwidth or slew-rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A neural network for noninvasive decomposition of surface EMG signals using Gaussian nodes
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The decomposition of surface EMG (electromyograms) signals into their constituent single fiber action potentials (SFAPs) is addressed. Generally, this problem is analytically not tractable and is computationally too complex to be reliable. It is demonstrated that it can be resolved by a specially designed neural network called the neural network with Gaussian nodes. Together with a modified back-propagation algorithm, a method of choosing initial conditions is presented. The significance of such solutions is that they allow a physician or medical researcher to observe the time behavior of SFAPs in a noninvasive manner for diagnostic purposes or other medical applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrating circuit design and formal verification
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The application of formal methods to the specification and design derivation of integrated circuits is addressed. The initial specification is expressed as an abstract relation between data tuples. This relation is a combination of conditional statements and associated data actions. Structural circuit descriptions are derived by step-wise application of proven laws to the specification while maintaining behavioral equivalence. This yields designs that are correct by construction. An example of a simple microprocessor design is used to illustrate the method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An approach to linear phase approximation that uses time domain constraints
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A design procedure for linear phase filters is presented. The ideal frequency-domain performance is transformed to the time domain. A realizable filter which has impulse-response zero crossings close to those of the ideal case is found. Computed results confirm the quality of this approximation method. The ideal zero crossings act as guides and give the desired control in both time and frequency domains.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Timing in systolic systems with variable minimum connection delays
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Mapping an originally delay-free dataflow graph onto a systolic hardware consisting of various programmable ALUs (arithmetic logic unit) and a programmable network connecting them will introduce variable extra delays between the processing nodes. To ensure successful mapping it will usually be necessary to increase some of the delays. An algorithm is introduced for calculating these delays and the position to add them. This algorithm was implemented in PicPEn, a programming environment created for the Picot system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New stability criteria for the nonuniform sampling digital phase-locked loops
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Stability criteria for digital nonuniform sampling zero-crossing phase-locked loops are derived. The functional nonlinear discrete-time equation on the S/sup 1/-circle manifold is used to describe the phase error process in a loop of any order. Disturbed N:1 phase entrainment is studied, where the perturbation is either the frequency offset or additional random noise and effects due to quantization. The class of loops with discontinuous characteristic of the phase detector is advocated as they exhibit fast acquisition, no matter what the initial phase error conditions are, for any order of loop. The notion of the covering space from the theory of dynamical systems is used to consider the dynamics of the loop on the S/sup 1/-circle manifold. The approach is extensible to include the fading of the input waveform, AM and PM modulation, and loop filters with variable coefficients.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A least-squares pole-zero algorithm in the frequency and Walsh domains with applications to speech representation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A spectral envelope matching technique is presented to allow coding of the mixed DFT-WHT parameters at lower rates. A least-squares (LS) pole-zero algorithm is derived in the frequency-domain. Pole-zero, as well as all-zero and all-pole, solutions can be obtained using the LS algorithm. The all-pole model is employed in this research to fit finite subsets of DFT components and WHT spectral components. The all-pole function, while characterized by real coefficients, carries location, magnitude, and phase information for accurate signal synthesis. Simulation results, using speech signals, are presented to demonstrate the performance of the algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dual independent cell generation
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A two-stage linear-time optimization algorithm is presented for dual independent layout styles. The first stage is based on a new tree representation of the complex gate. This tree representation allows complete flexibility in transistor order and takes complete advantage of the concept of delayed binding. The optimization algorithm is applicable to many VLSI layout styles. The algorithm is applied to the M/sup 3/ layout style, and examples of generated layouts are shown. Starting from a switching expression, the algorithm always produces an optimal solution, which includes an optimal transistor representation for the switching expression (first stage), and an optimal gate sequence such that the layout contains a minimum number of diffusion gaps (second stage).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RNS neural networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A type of perceptron based on a residue number system (RNS) implementation is introduced. Due to the scaling involved in the RNS, it operates with a particular periodic nonlinearity which increases its capability of problem solving. Two examples which clearly show that the RNS perceptron has better performance than the classical perceptron are presented. In both the examples the RNS perceptron solves a problem which is out of the possibility of the corresponding nonRNS perceptron.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On prime factors of nonsingular rational matrices
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An examination is made of the minimal factorization problem for square nonsingular rational matrices with an additional constraint that the dimensions of the factors are required to be the same as the original matrix. This dimensional constraint poses certain difficulties, and in fact it is known that the first degree minimal factorization is no longer possible in this case. In other words, the prime factors (matrices which cannot be factorized) can have degrees greater than 1. The main result of this work is to present a necessary condition for prime factor of nonsingular rational matrices with disjoint sets of poles and zeros. There are indications that this condition may also be sufficient.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Logical function and delay time extraction from MOS circuit data
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An algorithm to extract logical function and delay-time from CMOS circuit-level data is proposed. The resultant data from this algorithm is a logic-level circuit description. It is applied to conventional logic simulators. As a result, a large circuit can be simulated at once, and the time needed for simulation and verification is saved. The algorithm consists of three parts, network partitioning, extraction of logical function, and extraction of delay time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The advent of the signal microprocessor
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A software-controlled processor for analog signals, called the signal microprocessor (SMP), is described. The SMP is enabled by the high-speed buffer memory technology of acoustic charge transport (ACT) which stores samples of wideband signals as quantities of charge. The signal samples are processed in a massively parallel architecture which uses ultrasound to transport the samples from one processor to the next. In this high-speed computational engine, digitally programmable attenuators serve as multipliers and a summing bus is used as an accumulator. This architecture has demonstrated multiply-and-accumulate rates in excess of 45 billion operations per second. A digitally programmable 128-tap finite impulse response filter is described. This device may be used in each of the basic signal-processing functions of signal generation, extraction, modification, and characterization. Some SMP applications and examples are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed RC-filters with linearized MOS-transistors in CMOS technology
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two distributed RC filters (a low-pass and a bandpass) that use MOS transistors as distributed RC lines are presented. A scheme for compensating for nonlinearities in the MOSFET is used. Simulation results for a 2- mu m CMOS p-well process (MOSIS) are presented. High programmability is expected from two tuning points: the gain of the voltage amplifier to control the Q of the filters, and the DC bias of the MOSFETs to change omega /sub 0/. SPICE simulation results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Chaos in mutually coupled phase-locked loops
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is shown both by experiment and by computer simulation that two mutually coupled phase-locked loops (PLLs) can become chaotic when the two PLLs are operating in a marginal out-of-lock condition (that is, they are out of lock but very close to lock-in). The system is described by a fourth-order nonlinear autonomous equation. The power spectrum of the out-of-lock solution (close to lock-in) is observed to be a continuous broad band similar to that of a random signal. The largest Lyapunov exponent is found to be positive. This chaotic regime is observed over a large area of typical damping coefficients used in practical coupled PLL systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Compact template polynomials methodology in pattern recognition and parallel processing
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A polynomial approach is presented to the representation of binary, gray images for machine vision. It is shown that most of the standard image processing can be done by the template polynomial operations. Some operators which rely on the intrinsic properties of polynomials and can be done at a considerable advantage using the polynomial representation of images are developed. In particular, a parallel algorithm is developed by template decomposition; it uses the separability property of the template polynomial to reduce the time complexity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The neural network self-healing process by using a reconstructed sample space
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The inherent ability of neural networks to recover information when neurons in the network are damaged is discussed. This self-healing property is shown to exist in networks used for pattern recognition. The self-organizing feature map (SOFM) is the network used to study this topic. The SOFM has an efficient data compression technique that allows signal processing techniques to be used in recovering lost information from destroyed nodes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A lay-out level comparison of RNS and BNS systolic architectures for complex digital filtering
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Algorithms are developed to compute the number of active devices for residue number system (RNS) and binary number system (BNS) signal processing architectures. The precharged CMOS technology is used in order to build the filter architecture. The ROM lookup table and two's complement multiplier are used as the computational cells in the RNS and BNS, respectively. A direct implementation transversal systolic filter architecture is considered in RNS and BNS algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A greedier detailed router
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A switchbox/channel routing heuristic called greedier is presented. It is a column-sweep-based heuristic which combines features from existing approaches with new features of its own to generate substantially improved solutions. Tests on switchbox benchmarks show that the heuristic gives very good results in terms of the number of vias, total interconnection length, and CPU time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some properties of continuous-time and switched capacitor filters based on current charge and voltage simulation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A general formulation for switched-capacitor or continuous-time filter architectures is used to make a comparison of the properties of the various architectures within a common framework. The performance parameters considered are the sensitivity of response to component parameter variations and the extent to which nodal voltage scaling in order to maximize signal handling capability can be applied. Some examples are presented and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testing of zipper CMOS logic circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method for testing zipper CMOS circuits is presented. A gate-level model for the circuit is derived, and a single stuck-at fault test set for the model is obtained. Vectors are rearranged in the test set so that it can be used to detect single stuck-open and stuck-on faults in addition to stuck-at faults in the zipper CMOS circuit. Faults in the drive circuit are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Linear-phase multirate IIR filters
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Wave digital filter studies are used to design multirate IIR (infinite-impulse response) linear-phase filters. The resulting structures have low sensitivity to element values. A method for analyzing multirate filters in the time domain is described and used to produce a number of design examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An iterative method for transient analysis in nonuniform transmission line
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Integral equations of nonuniform lossy lines are presented. Parameters of the line vary according to arbitrary, sufficiently smooth functions. The iterative method (successive approximations) of solution of integral equations for some classes of the line is presented. It gives a closed form of first-order approximation of the voltage and current distribution along the line. Power and cosine lines are considered as examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Monolithic GaAs programmable parallel-to-serial and serial-to-parallel converters
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: GaAs monolithic parallel-to-serial (P/S) and serial-to-parallel (S/P) converters which provide significant improvements in speed and power performance over previously reported devices are described. The converters are designed with an architecture that provides automatic frame synchronization, simple cascadability, and low power dissipation. Each chip provides an output clock in phase with the output data to facilitate postprocessing. The P/S and S/P chips operate at data rates of 1.9 Gb/s and 2.1 Gb/s, respectively, and each requires less than 120 mW of power. The chips are implemented with DCFL using a version of ITT's multifunction self-aligned gate fabrication process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient DAG synthesis (VLSI logic design)
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method is presented for synthesis in the presence of arbitrary conditional branches. The synthesis system, DPE, is based on the simulated annealing algorithm. DPE translates the initial specification into an internal, graph-oriented representation. Simulated annealing is used to apply compaction transformations to the graph. A user-specified cost function, which includes registers, arithmetic and logic units (ALUs), control steps, and interconnect requirements, is used to evaluate the effect of the transformations and the quality of the resulting data path. This approach produces very-high-quality results in a reasonable time. DPE was enhanced to accept arbitrary program DAGs as input. This required four modifications to the standard basic block synthesis technique: resource sharing, statement coloring, multiple definitions, and addition of control information and dependencies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of systems subject to parameter uncertainties: application of interval analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The use of interval analysis techniques is proposed to establish estimates of system performance (e.g. envelopes of time response and frequency response). The results constitute generalizations of previously established work. Systems described by linear or nonlinear ordinary difference equations endowed with more than one parameter belonging to intervals are addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Toward the use of set-membership identification in efficient training of feedforward neural networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The application of the theory of set-membership identification to the development of efficient learning algorithms for neural networks is discussed. Some results relevant to the application of the method to nonlinear feedforward networks are presented. The techniques discussed have the potential to significantly improve the efficiency of teaching neural networks by employing novel data selection criteria based on set-theoretic constraints.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Classified vector quantization of images using texture analysis
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new VQ-based image coding method, classified vector quantization using texture analysis (CVQ-TA) is proposed. The most notable differences between CVQ-TA and CVQ are: (1) the classification in CVQ-TA operates in the transform domain by means of texture analysis, and (2) product-code vector quantization is used to reduce the complexity increasing with the subblock size. Because of these characteristics, CVQ-TA can be applied for large block size (8*8 or 16*16), which is more efficient for block coding. Simulation results show that CVQ-TA can give a good visual perceptual quality.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Heterojunction bipolar transistors for high speed integrated circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The unique characteristics of heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs), their fabrication, state-of-the-art performance and applications are discussed. The future directions of HBT research and commercialization, including new material systems and advanced device structures, are addressed. HBTs are compared with other devices which operate in the GHz frequency range. These devices include bipolar junction transistors and field effect transistors. A discussion of HBT materials is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An extended 1-D assignment problem: net assignment in gate matrix layout
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A formulation for the net assignment problem in gate matrix layout is presented. A problem called the extended one-dimensional assignment problem is defined. A heuristic algorithm for solving this extended one-dimensional assignment problem is proposed. Since the net assignment problem in gate matrix is the extended one-dimensional assignment problem exactly, this algorithm is applied to the net assignment. The time complexity of the algorithm is bounded by O(m*n/sup 2/), where n is the number of nets and m is the sum of the number of vertical diffusion runs and the number of gates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scattering parameters and CAD of microwave E-plane double metal filters
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A computer direct optimizing design technique for E-plane double metal sheet filters is developed, based on the scattering parameter method which takes into account the higher-order mode coupling and strip thickness. Thus, the characteristics of the filters are improved greatly. A double metal sheet filter in X-band has been fabricated and tested. Because coupling of the higher-order modes in the resonator is taken into account, the design method is more efficient and accurate for the practical application. In order to shorten the total computing time, the first 10 modes only need to be considered for the optimizing program. Good agreement between theory and measurement results has been obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel algorithm for solving nonlinear networks
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An efficient algorithm has been developed for analyzing nonlinear electronic networks. The algorithm generates a signal-flow graph for any electronic network with no restrictions on topology or types of nonlinearities. The network can be configured on a system of parallel processors, resulting in a very efficient algorithm. The basic algorithm suffers from instabilities under certain conditions, and a method of ensuring stability is described. Examples are given of nonlinear networks analyzed on a system of parallel processors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bezier formulation of multistep algorithms
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Predictor-based integration formulas are presented by formulating the solution function as a vectored value Bernstein polynomial, namely a Bezier function. The Bezier function subdivision theorem leads to a predictor evaluation algorithm for the next solution point using de Casteljau's iterative control vertex generation technique. It is shown that the convergence of the algorithms is a consequence of the use of Bernstein uniform approximation basis and that the de Casteljau predictor evaluation scheme leads to a computationally simple estimate of the local truncation error.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Zero modules for systems over rings
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: This study centers on some of the results given by F. Bostwick et al. (J. Control Optim., vol.25, no.1, p.86-99, Jan. 1987) which connect zeros of the Rosenbrock system matrix with zeros of the transfer function. It is shown that some of these results can be obtained for linear time-invariant systems over an arbitrary ring. In particular, the Omega -zero and Gamma -zero modules for systems over arbitrary rings are defined. The kernel and cokernel of the transfer function, not necessarily proper, and the Rosenbrock system map are shown to be canonically isomorphic. These isomorphisms are embedded into a commutative exact diagram. The corresponding results extended to the Omega -level and to the Gamma -level are then examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation of the use of analog design methods for the integration of a high frequency mixed analog digital fiber optic receiver
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The design, simulation, fabrication, and evaluation of a fiber optic digital signal receiver is discussed. The receiver recovers a four-level digitally encoded signal from a fiber optic channel through a photodiode. It is integrated on a very-high-frequency bipolar oxide-isolated process and operates at 200 M samples/s.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Randomly perturbed array processing with optimum integral nulling approach
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Pattern integral synthesis is used in an optimal sense to achieve a broadband gain response in a linear array with equispaced isotropic sensors which is subject to random variations of array weights and sensor positions. The expectations of integrals of array space-frequency and power responses are analyzed and used to find an optimum weight vector which generates a broadband gain response in a specified spatial region. A set of narrowband gains within a specified region, pattern derivative, or integral is used to achieve a broadband gain response. Without loss of generality, it is assumed that the expected sensor positions are confined to a one-dimensional space, the directions of incoming signals are confined to a two-dimensional space, and the sensor positions vary randomly in a three-dimensional space.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Seismic inversion by the combined use of predictive and semblance techniques
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The combination of predictive and semblance methods is the basis of several techniques of seismic inversion. A method for estimating the velocities of the compressional, shear, and Stoneley waves is proposed and applied to synthetic cases. The results obtained with eight of them are summarized and are quite satisfactory. The number of receivers in all the cases considered is eight, and the distance between them is 15 cm. The order of the Prony model is chosen to be three. One of the eight cases is illustrated in more detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A unified approach to the design of canonical integrated ladder filters
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A method is introduced for designing stable, active integrated ladder filters with canonic numbers of op amps from a class of hitherto problematic transfer functions including bandstop and even-order elliptic functions. A variety of familiar parasitic-insensitive ladder structures can be produced by matrix methods while retaining the low sensitivity properties expected of passive simulations. The method is applicable to active-RC, switched-capacitor, and digital technologies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mechanical aspects of second level packaging interconnection methods
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Mechanical modeling of the main structural categories in second-level packaging is discussed, covering leadless chip carriers, pin-grid arrays, and flatpacks. Operational stress considerations focus on thermal loads, but manufacturing, handling, and dynamics are also considered. Development, test, and field conditions are related through mechanical analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An intuitive behavioral modeling language for mixed signal ASIC simulation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An intuitive behavioral modelling language is introduced within the circuit simulator URECA. The URECA language is constructed using operators as extensions to the netlist format commonly found in analog simulators such as SPICE. The operators have been developed to model input/output behavior in mixed signal circuits and describe common analog behavioral qualities. Several mixed analog/digital circuit examples are simulated using this language, and the accuracy and processing speed are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: InP opto-electronic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The requirements of InP opto-electronic ICs (OEIC) are discussed, and the progress being made in meeting these requirements is reviewed. Advantages and problems associated with the integration of OEIC elemental devices (e.g. laser diodes, photodetectors, and transistors) are discussed. The progress on two circuits, laser-transmitters and photodetector-receivers, is reviewed to demonstrate the integration of these elemental devices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimum DSP multiprocessor architecture for efficient execution of the fast transversal filter
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The design and development of an efficient multiprocessor system to implement the fast transversal filter (FTF) using commercially available digital signal processors (DSPs) is presented. The system is designed with some flexibility in it to be able to run other commonly used adaptive signal-processing algorithms. The FTF algorithm is analyzed, noting sequential characteristics and heavy computational bottlenecks that limit the speed at which the algorithm runs. The algorithm is speared to couple of data independent partitions which were data dependent by data flow concept. Parallelisms within the FTF and within its vector computations are the target of speedup efforts. The design is chosen to maximize speedup and minimize interprocessor communication, all with the minimum number of processors and simplest control logic. A prototype of the system using four Motorola DSP56001 fixed-point DSPs is discussed. The system has a speedup factor of nearly 4 over the single-DSP implementations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quadrature mirror filter design by Chebyshev approximation
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The design of a half-band filter for subband coding systems is discussed. The characteristics of both the time and frequency responses of the half-band filter are used in order to reduce the computation time and increase the computation accuracy. The constraint for such a filter is that the even terms of its impulse response must be zero in order to meet the requirement of a uniform frequency response for the whole system. An algorithm based on the Chebyshev approximation that utilizes only odd-symmetry polynomials for frequency interpolation to meet the required frequency response of the half-band filter is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Provocative topics on linear integrated circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A discussion is presented of the following topics: relative priorities, check lists, design reviews, design rule checks, digitally computerized simulation, analog computer simulations, breadboards, test strategies, and metal-mask options. These are demonstrated to be valuable for enhancing the probability of good results in high-volume linear integrated circuits (ICs).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generation of network functions in symbolic form by using the mixed diagonal node admittance matrix
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The mixed diagonal node admittance matrix is introduced. Its application to the inversion of the node admittance matrix is discussed. A simple method for obtaining network functions in symbolic form is presented. The method is based on obtaining the network function for various parameter values.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the relationship between external and internal stability of linear time-varying systems
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: New analytical definitions of stabilizability and detectability for a linear time-varying discrete-time system are given. It is shown that, if a linear system has these properties and has reachability and observability matrices with bounded pseudoinverses, then external or bounded-input-bounded-output (BIBO) stability of the system is equivalent to internal or uniform asymptotic stability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A top-down built-in self-test design in VLSI testing
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A top-down design of test generation and response analysis for built-in self-test (BIST) is proposed. The design procedure is computationally efficient for test generation, and produces test generation circuitry with low hardware overhead. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated by detailed comparisons of the results with those obtained with existing techniques. For response analysis, a delay redundancy check is proposed to improve the failure rate of a vertical and horizontal redundancy check fault-detection scheme. In combination with the two-signature scheme, the frequency of aliasing is reduced to one in 2/sup 4n/ for an n-input, m-output circuit under test, where 2/sup n/>m.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An estimation theoretic approach to the asynchronous detection of PSK signals
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An algorithm is presented for smoothing data that are modeled piecewise by linear state-space equations from measurements corrupted by additive noise. Its main feature is the combination of a Markov model with Kalman filtering (KF) techniques in order to smooth and segment the data within the regions and detect the instant when the transitions occur. Particular attention is given to the filtering and segmentation of sinusoidal signals with periodic phase shifts, and the algorithm is shown to operate as a PSK detector.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A framework for analog circuit verification
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A computer environment, Nectar, that integrates an array of circuit verification capabilities in a comprehensive program is presented. Nectar emphasizes design tasks and hides the idiosyncrasies of individual tools. The components and features of the analog design framework are presented. An implementation of the rule-based expert system component of the framework results in an over tenfold increase in speed, thus giving the environment additional corrective capabilities. Another major component described is a rule editor, which simplifies the extension of the knowledge base of Nectar.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a class of multidimensional recursive digital filters using transformation techniques
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: It is shown that stable 3-D recursive digital filters with low-sensitivity ladder realizations can be derived from 1-D analog prototypes via spectral transformation. A major advantage of the design approach is that the initial approximation method is carried out in the analog domain utilizing the available methods, design tables, and techniques. Conversion to the discrete domain is carried out through a set of closed-form design formulas and, thus, does not require the cumbersome approach of iterative methods of optimization. The stability of the resulting digital filter reverts to that of ensuring that the employed multivariable reactance function is stable. Thus, the stability of the designed filter is guaranteed as long as all coefficients of this reactance function are positive real constants. The design method can easily be extended to realize a similar class of multidimensional recursive digital filters. Zero-phase filtering is easily obtained with the cost of only one first-octant filter realization. Another feature of the realization technique is that it lends itself to generating digital filters with tunable characteristics. By appropriately changing the parameters of the transformation function, one can adjust bandwidth along each dimension as well as the convexity of the passband hyperplane. Nevertheless, the shape of the passband region closely follows the characteristics of the multivariable reactance function. Therefore, the shape of the passband region is not completely tunable. Another drawback of this technique is that online processing for real-time data is not possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On nonessential singularities of the second kind in T/sup 2/U for 3-D digital filters
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The problems of linear form nonessential singularities of the second kind in T/sup 2/U for three-dimensional digital filters are discussed. Based on the Weierstrass theorem of multidimensional complex analysis, the existence criteria are obtained. Some basic properties for these kinds of singularities are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Realization of Boolean functions by perceptron algorithm
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Summary form only given. A two-step design procedure is proposed so that any Boolean function can be realized by the reliable perceptron algorithm. The first step is the learning phase. In the second step, the outputs are simply connected to an OR-gate, a perceptron by itself.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive system identification method on bispectrum
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: An adaptive technique for the identification of a linear system which is driven by white non-Gaussian noise is proposed. The system can be a nonminimum phase system. The adaptive identification technique is a least-mean-square type algorithm, and it is obtained by using the higher order cumulants of the system output. A simulation example is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time-frequency estimation from either signal domain-implementation on a RISC system
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A Wigner-distribution-based spectral estimation is optimized for high-level-language implementation on a reduced-instruction-set-computer (RISC) architecture. Traditionally, time-frequency estimators have relied on time histories for the input. The implementation presented allows for equivalent transformation to the t-w plane given either time or frequency input data. The estimator employs a generalized form of the WD and is developed at the algorithm level to offer both flexibility and computational efficiency. Several DFT alternatives including the radix-2 FFT, radix-4 FFT, SRFFT, WFTA, and PFA are investigated in terms of relative computational delays versus a floating-point addition-time-to-multiply-time ratio.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Approximative threshold-calculation of a PLL-FM-demodulator with bandpass-limiter
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The author's method (Proc. 1988 IEEE Int. Symp. Circ. Syst., p.595-8) for easily and rapidly calculating and optimizing the FM-threshold-level of a phase-locked-loop FM demodulator is extended by including a bandpass-limiter in the preselection system, based on a new threshold-criterion for the phase-error variance. It requires only a numerical integration and a zero-search instead of solving a nonlinear differential equation in the time domain; this reduces the computation time on a CRAY vector computer for a complete threshold curve from a few thousand seconds to a few seconds in all cases of practical interest. Nevertheless, the results of both theories are in good agreement within about 1 dB as well as with experimental data within the limits of measuring accuracy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Exact equivalence of iterative pre-filtering and IQML
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The iterative prefiltering algorithm of Steiglitz and McBride (1965) is rederived in a new form that demonstrates its exact equivalence to the iterative quadratic maximum-likelihood (IQML) algorithm. Since the IQML method was originally formulated to solve a multiple measurement case, an extended version of iterative prefiltering applicable to the multiple measurement case is also stated and shown to be equivalent to the general form of IQML.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data compressor decompressor IC
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The data compressor decompressor (DCD) IC, a VLSI implementation of a version of the Lempel-Ziv (L-Z) compression algorithm, is discussed. The IC is suitable for high-speed, lossless compression of digital data such as text and images. The single-pass lossless compression scheme adapts to the statistics of the data being processed. The authors outline the L-Z compression method, illustrate a solution to its search requirement, and discuss the chip architecture and features.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A concurrent solution for large systems of linear equations
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: A concurrent, iterative, algorithm is described which can solve any very large linear system of equations that is nonsingular. The method has been implemented in the Occam 2 language and tested satisfactorily on an Inmos Transputer Evaluation Module. Although the multicomputer system does not use memory circuitry as efficiently on single-instruction-multiple-data (SIMD) tasks as does the multiprocessor shared memory design, it avoids the problems of contention, synchronization, and deadlock.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Threshold of stability and test procedure for 2-D scattering Hurwitz polynomials
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: Based on the concept of threshold of stability, a procedure to test a given two-dimensional polynomial to see if it is a discrete scattering Hurwitz polynomial is presented. In this procedure, the only values to be computed are the derivatives of a given polynomial at its zeros on the distinguished boundary of the unit bidisc.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of a neural net expert system in the presence of don't care and don't know features
publicationTitle: IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
abstract: The implementation of a neural network acting as an expert system is discussed. In some cases a particular feature may not be appropriate to describe a particular object (don't care condition) or a particular feature cannot be extracted or is missing (don't know feature). It is shown how the traditional feedforward neural network cannot be trained on these types of features, and an alternate structure is shown that is optimal when the features are discrete and independent and errors are independent. The structure is highly regular. It is shown how to implement the network using operational amplifiers and logic gates. The application to a real-world problem of identifying ordnances is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Subspace-based approach for circuit simulation
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An approach to dealing with the very large circuit simulation problem is presented. This approach is a subspace-based method of solving a system of equations in the linear equation solution level cataloged in the direct solution method. The subspace-based approach is developed by the inspection of the solution errors of a system of equations These solution errors respect the latency within a very large circuit. The convergence, accuracy, efficiency, and storage are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New algorithms of extrapolation and spectral estimation for discrete band-limited signals based on Fourier transform
publicationTitle: 1990 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two algorithms of extrapolation and spectral estimation for discrete bandlimited signals are proposed that are based on Fourier transform. The two algorithms, the matrix algorithm and the iterative FFT algorithm, can provide more accurate spectral estimates and better extrapolation performance than other algorithms developed for discrete bandlimited signals with a smooth spectrum.
